newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-U.S. OPEN HAS HART, AS ALTERNATE LAUNCHES CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-U.S. OPEN HAS HART, AS ALTERNATE LAUNCHES CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: The U.S. Open, whose testing conditions have broken the heart of many a contender, launched its 97th edition of the championship with a Hart at the helm.

Alternate Steve Hart got a wake-up call at 6:15 a.m. from a U.S. Golf Association official asking if he could get to the course in time for a 7 a.m tee time to take the place of Brad Bryant, who withdrew because of a case of the flu.

The 27-year-old Hart hustled down to the course -- he needed to have a courtesy car pick him up since he had left his rental car keys in a work-out van on Wednesday -- and joined the first group teeing off at Congressional Country Club.
"I hit first. I hit the first ball of the Open. Can you imagine that?" said Hart, sporting a bloody nick on his chin where a hasty job of shaving had left its mark.

A self-described veteran of "every tour except the ladies' tour," Hart bogeyed three holes on the front side to make the turn at 38. He nearly neutralised three more bogeys on the inward nine by posting a pair of birdies and finished the round at four-over 74.
"I just hope I can play better tomorrow," said Hart, who added that having two boys at home, one aged 2 and the other 9 months, had prepared him to be able to rush into action at the early hour.
"I'll feel better about not wasting the spot," said Hart, who is assured of at least a $1,000 pay day for competing.
